stellar masses derived from broadband colors agree reasonably well with masses derived from spectroscopic features (rms ~ 0.2 dex) and that these masses are also in reasonable agreement with dynamical ones.
broadband colors can be used to estimate stellar masses of galaxies with a precision of 0.15-0.2 dex, and with an accuracy of ~0.3 dex.

(a) the stellar masses of SDSS galaxies estimated from their broadband colors are in good agreement with masses derived from spectroscopic analysis and dynamical modeling; (b) the differences between masses from spectroscopic features and those from broadband colors correlate with Ha emission strength, while this correlation is not present for broadband colors and dynamical masses; (c) the scatter of stellar mass estimates based on spectroscopic features is significantly smaller than that of dynamical masses, but the systematic differences between the two are comparable

broadband color stellar mass estimates are reliable for galaxies in the local universe and at high redshift, while the spectroscopic method is reliable for galaxies in a certain mass-metallicity regime.

The main takeaway from our work is that

broadband mass estimates based on a large wavelength coverage, a large range of ages and metallicities, and an appropriate range of dust extinctions are reliable to a level that can be used to study galaxy evolution.
